subject: DataScale MSA / Order Form — Clarify output ownership & training license
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Park <jennifer.park@datascale.com>
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft MSA + OF — initial send

Hi Jennifer,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Attached are the MSA and Order Form drafts with our standard commercial positions (see attachments). Per our conversation you flagged two priority items: (1) the ownership language for model outputs, and (2) the customer training/feedback license.

Quick ask: could you confirm whether DataScale intends to retain exclusive rights to generated outputs, or will you accept a non-exclusive license to operate and productize results? That will determine the Order Form language we propose.

Next steps I propose:
- You and procurement review the attached redlines and return counterpoints
- If you have language you'd prefer for output ownership, send it back and we'll loop legal
- If there's urgency, we can schedule a 30-min call with legal this week

Attachments (stubs):
- DataScale_MSA_redlines_20270402.pdf (annotated MSA)
- OrderForm_v2_track_changes.docx (Order Form w/ proposed output clause)

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0148

From: Jennifer Park <jennifer.park@datascale.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Yang <michael.yang@datascale.com>, procurement@datascale.com
Date: 2027-04-02T11:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + OF — initial send

Ben —

Thanks for sending these over. Procurement and legal here reviewed quickly and attached a marked PDF with our initial redlines. Two summary points from our side:

1) Output ownership: our product team expects to own derivative outputs created by our users (we need exclusive rights to re-sell features built on top of generated content).
2) Training/use of feedback: we can agree to allow redwood to improve models on aggregated anonymized telemetry, but we need a strict carve-out for any content we mark as "sensitive" (PII, customer copyrighted material).

We attached DataScale_MSA_redlines_20270402.pdf (with comments). Procurement would like to understand whether your suggested language for the feedback license can be scoped by tag or label rather than broad reservation.

Can you have legal propose alternate text for both areas? Procurement indicated they may need to escalate to their general counsel if we can't find middle ground.

Jennifer Park
Sr. Contracts Manager | DataScale Inc.
jennifer.park@datascale.com

Attachment: DataScale_MSA_redlines_20270402.pdf

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Park <jennifer.park@datascale.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-03T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + OF — clarify desired outcomes

Jennifer —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the annotated PDF. Looping in Laura (legal) and Marissa (customer success/product) so we can respond with precise alternate language. A few notes from product/GT:

- We understand DataScale's desire to productize outputs; we typically offer a graded approach:
  * Exclusive ownership for Customer-curated datasets (e.g., a trained model snapshot built solely from customer proprietary data)
  * Non-exclusive, perpetual license for standard generated outputs produced by the service
- For training/use of feedback, we can implement label-based opt-outs (customer can tag data as "no-train") and provide telemetry exports so you can validate what was used

Laura — could you propose specific language that allows DataScale to claim exclusivity for final product components while protecting Redwood's ability to operate and improve the service? Also please highlight any commercial impacts (pricing/ops) if we accept exclusivity.

If it helps, Ben — please propose availability for a 30-minute legal sync on Friday (I can join).

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Jennifer Park <jennifer.park@datascale.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-04T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + OF — proposed alternate language

Hi all —

Thanks for looping me in. I reviewed the DataScale redlines and drafted two candidate clauses (below) that aim to bridge positions while preserving Redwood's operating model. Inline notes attached as a PDF — see OrderForm_v2_track_changes.docx for tracked language.

Summary (high level):
- Candidate A (Customer-friendly, commercial trade-off):
  * Customer receives exclusive ownership of "Customer Outputs" defined as final, human-reviewed product artifacts that are (i) generated by the Service and (ii) identified in a Delivery Schedule as Product Artifacts.
  * Redwood retains a non-exclusive, perpetual license to use non-identifiable, aggregated Outputs for product improvement and internal analytics.
  * Training carve-out: Customer may tag data "no-train"; any untagged data may be used in aggregated form. This option reduces operational burden but requires a 10% surcharge on committed capacity to cover caching & isolation costs.

- Candidate B (Redwood-preferred, operationally simpler):
  * Customer receives a non-exclusive license to Outputs sufficient for downstream use and commercialization, subject to attribution and audit rights.
  * Redwood retains broad rights to use anonymized Outputs and Feedback for model improvement; Customer may request a locked dataset build for an additional fee (one-time).

Questions for DataScale:
- Do you have a short list of "Product Artifacts" that must be exclusive? Naming examples helps us scope the Delivery Schedule.
- Is tagging-based opt-out acceptable operationally, or do you require a policy enforced at the network/VPC level (more costly)?

Attached: OrderForm_v2_track_changes.docx (tracked changes + two clause options).

If agreeable, I'd recommend we present Candidate A as the "compromise" option with the surcharge and Candidate B as our fallback. Happy to discuss on a call — suggest Friday 4/06 11:00 PT.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0223

Attachment: OrderForm_v2_track_changes.docx

From: Jennifer Park <jennifer.park@datascale.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Yang <michael.yang@datascale.com>, procurement@datascale.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-06T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + OF — next steps

Laura/Tessa —

Thanks for the clear options and the tracked document. DataScale likes Candidate A conceptually, but procurement needs clarity on the surcharge band and an example Delivery Schedule. Two quick items to keep moving:

1) Can Redwood share a short sample Delivery Schedule with 2–3 example "Product Artifacts" (e.g., "customer-curated training snapshot", "exported model weights", "finalized knowledge base bundle")?
2) For the tagging opt-out: procurement prefers a tagging API + audit log export (so they can reconcile). Will Redwood commit to weekly audit exports for tagged data used in training?

If you can provide the sample schedule and confirm weekly audit exports, procurement will run this to GC. We're tentatively scheduling a short call next week to finalize. Please send updated attachments when ready.

Best,
Jennifer Park
Sr. Contracts Manager | DataScale Inc.
jennifer.park@datascale.com
